_comment: The most period-legible garment in the menu. Two stripes down a sleeve and an elasticated cuff date a frame on their own, without a single word about how the picture looks. Note what is NOT here: no weather, no place, no time of day. climate below is the machine-readable channel for all of that, and checkCompatibility reads it -- the prose must not. REWRITTEN 2026-08-27 to read as sportswear rather than leisurewear, WITHOUT touching the period: it is zipped rather than hanging open, it has its matching pants, and the chest crest is gone. That crest was the single most leisure-coded thing in the line and the model drew it far larger than 'small' -- job 20260824-114051-4209a6 came back with a gold heraldic badge that reads country club, which is the opposite of trackside. Every negative is unchanged except one added for the same reason.
label: Tracksuit jacket
wardrobe: a full-zip tracksuit jacket in navy with two white stripes running down the outside of each sleeve, a stand collar zipped to the throat, elasticated cuffs and hem, and matching navy track pants carrying the same two stripes down the outside leg, worn over a plain white t-shirt
